name: De-illumination

global_influences.evidence: De-illumination was explicitly formed with the vision of introducing symphonic rock/symphonic metal to Bangladeshi music, a genre founder Sazzad Arefeen had been studying since 1999 — a deliberate, research-driven import of a specific global metal subgenre rather than incidental exposure.

local_adaptation_notes: Co-founded by Sazzad Arefeen (who had studied symphonic metal since 1999) and Shams Mansoor Ghani, then Warfaze's keyboardist, De-illumination represents a direct lineage connection from Bangladesh's heavy metal founding generation (via Warfaze) into a deliberately imported subgenre; the band's name itself articulates a philosophical stance — rejecting 'illuminated exterior, full of imposed knowledge and prejudice' in favor of embracing one's inner light or darkness — giving the symphonic-metal import an explicitly localized conceptual framing.
sound_evolution_summary: Formative period (2006): formed with the explicit mission of introducing symphonic rock/metal to Bangladesh, drawing on Shams Mansoor Ghani's Warfaze pedigree. Pre-album period (2008): appeared on two mixed compilation albums (Dabanol, Rage-1) to build recognition ahead of a full-length release. Debut album period (2010): অনিবার্য (Inevitable) delivered the band's first full-length symphonic metal statement, cementing its status as Bangladesh's first symphonic rock/metal act.
concert_culture_notes: Specific concert/festival data not yet documented in available sources — flagged for further research; the band's genre-pioneer status (first symphonic rock/metal act in Bangladesh) likely positioned it within the same progressive/heavy-metal festival circuit as Artcell, Warfaze and Cryptic Fate.
listener_community_notes: Occupies a distinct niche within the Progressive/Metal genre ecosystem as Bangladesh's specifically symphonic-metal pioneer, appealing to listeners seeking orchestral/keyboard-driven textures beyond the guitar-centric progressive metal of Artcell or the straight heavy metal of Warfaze and Cryptic Fate.
